thesis.question: What does this part argue, and in what order should its chapters be read?
thesis.claim: Part IX argues that the dated public record of six marketplace cases supports the book's sharing pattern only up to the product layer: sharing the uniform layers held up while product convergence is a separate, riskier bet; every shared dependency must survive a change of owner; and the vertical lessons sit in contracts and models. Because those lessons are only as strong as their evidence, the cases are read under rules that keep dated fact, the author's reading and labeled inference apart, with fictional Veldmark only in each case's final comparison, and in an order that runs from whole groups to single verticals, starting with Adevinta.
thesis.disputed_by: The view that real groups' histories teach little about architecture, because each turn was a capital or market decision, so the cases are company profiles a reader may skim in any order and cite at whatever strength suits the argument.
thesis.so_what: A reader who accepts it reads each case statement as fact, reading or inference and cites it at that strength, opens the case that speaks to the decision in front of them, and ends Part IX able to say which of the book's patterns the record supports, which it only fails to contradict, and where it is silent.
thesis.how_why: The six cases bought, merged, shared, sold and retreated in public. Adevinta's 2023 plan to turn two generalist platforms into one was reversed by 2025, and AVIV's 2021 goal of 'a European real estate marketplace' gave way to local autonomy; eBay's 2020–2021 sale and Adevinta's 2025 break-up turned shared platforms into transitional-service terms and separation costs; Zillow Offers wound down in November 2021. The evidence is uneven: Adevinta published a great deal, eBay Classifieds almost nothing as a group, and AVIV no engineering material at all.

supporting_claims.claim: Part IX's cases are read under stricter evidence rules than Parts I–VIII: every statement is a dated fact, the author's reading or a labeled inference, the depth of each case follows its evidence, and Veldmark appears only in each case's final comparison.
The six cases are read from whole groups to single verticals, starting with Adevinta, and each is the one to open for a recognizable decision.

Read side by side, the six records give the part's three lessons: share the uniform layers and treat product convergence as a separate bet, design every shared dependency to survive a change of owner, and carry the vertical lessons in contracts and models.
The cases test the chapters the book's argument rests on and Veldmark's 2027 choices, without extending the scenario, and the toolkit turns the book's decisions into templates.

flow.rationale: The page opens on the argument the book closed and the question Part IX puts to it, then sets the evidence rules before any case is named, because every row that follows is a dated fact and the reader must know how to weigh it. It narrows to the six cases in reading order with the decision that sends a reader to each, then sets them side by side so the three lessons of the KEY POINTS can be read across the rows. It then shows, in one place, where the fictional Veldmark appears and the 2027 choices the cases hold against the record, widens once to the chapters the cases test and the toolkit, and ends with a short synthesis, the part's three-way test and the hand-off to Adevinta. Put the comparison before the chapter table and its rows arrive before the reader knows the cases; put the evidence rules after the tables and their dated facts are read before the reader knows what a date means; split Veldmark's place from its choices and the reader meets the fiction twice, far apart (both round-3 flow readers); put Veldmark before the cases and the fiction is met before the real record it is tested against.
